Documentation → Monitoring & Analysis → Path Diagnostics

Path Diagnostics — localise a broken service

Name one FortiWeb server policy or FortiADC virtual server and Path Diagnostics walks a ten-rung ladder — appliance, object, DNS, front door, certificate, pool, backends, network path, decision, WAF — stopping at the first layer that fails and naming it with evidence. Read-only; can be switched off site-wide.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsmonitoring.view monitoring.probe_free users.manage
📍 WhereGlobal, FortiWeb and FortiADC ADOMs: Operations → Troubleshooting → Path Diagnostics (URL /scout/)

What is it?#

When someone says "this service is broken", Path Diagnostics answers which layer is broken? You pick an appliance and name one published object — a FortiWeb server policy or a FortiADC virtual server — and Path Diagnostics walks a ladder of checks in dependency order. The first rung that fails is the verdict; every rung below it is marked not walked. Path Diagnostics is read-only: it issues only GET-type requests and never writes configuration.

Path Diagnostics can be switched off for the whole site; the menu entry then stays visible but disabled, with the reason. A user without the permission Path Diagnostics needs does not see the entry at all.

ℹ️Note

Renamed on 2026-10-14: this page was called Scout until then. The name Scout now belongs to the AI assistant (see Scout). Only the labels changed: the URL /scout/, bookmarks and the audit action scout.walk are the same.

What does it do?#

Rung Layer Question Observed from
0 Appliance is the box itself fit to serve? the appliance
1 Object does the policy exist and is it enabled? the appliance
2 Name does the published name resolve? this node
3 Front door does the VIP answer, and which phase is slow? this node
4 Certificate is the presented chain valid today? this node
5 Pool does the device have members behind this object? the appliance
6 Backends can the backends be reached, and from where? the appliance
7 Path firewall, reset, or routing? the collector (FortiAnalyzer)
8 Decision is the appliance deciding or relaying? this node
9 WAF is the profile blocking this traffic? the appliance

Each rung returns pass, fail, warn, unknown (could not look) or skipped (below a failure), with a headline and evidence. The summary is either Fault localised at layer N (Layer), observed from … or, when nothing failed, a statement of how many rungs were probed — a walk with rungs that could not be probed is reported as a partial walk, never as healthy.

Requirements#

  • Path Diagnostics switched on (Settings → Path Diagnostics → Settings, Path Diagnostics is available).
  • A FortiWeb or FortiADC appliance visible in the current ADOM.
  • For rung 7 (Path): a FortiAnalyzer registered and visible; otherwise that rung is unknown.
  • For the appliance vantage on backends: SSH credentials, and Use SSH ticked.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

  • Using Path Diagnostics: the legacy view gate — any read permission, for example monitoring.view; all system profiles have it.
  • Path Diagnostics settings (Settings → Path Diagnostics), including the site-wide on/off switch: users.manage (Administrator) — both to see the tab and to save. Any other user gets 403 on save.
  • A Published host you type is checked by host and port: it is dialled only if the appliance publishes that pair — its own address on its management or SSH port, or one of the VIPs / front ends in its configuration or live listing on the port that service is served on (or its scheme's default port) — unless you hold monitoring.probe_free or users.manage, the same rule as the certificate inspector and transaction tracer. Leaving the field blank (host derived from the object's VIP) needs no extra permission. Every host is also checked against SATOM's outbound-target rules (metadata addresses and some ports are refused).
  • The menu entry: Operations → Troubleshooting → Path Diagnostics is drawn only for a user who may open the page. A user without that permission does not see it (it is not shown as switched off). When Path Diagnostics is switched off for the site, the entry is shown to everyone, disabled, with the tooltip Path Diagnostics is switched off for this site (Settings → Path Diagnostics → Availability).

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: a typed Published host outside the appliance's own addresses and VIPs now needs monitoring.probe_free (or users.manage), and saving the settings needs users.manage; Viewer and Operator can no longer do either.

ℹ️Note

Changed on 2026-10-14: the typed Published host is checked as a host-and-port pair. Before, a host the appliance published authorised every port on it, so the appliance's own address with an arbitrary port was dialled without monitoring.probe_free.

How to use#

  1. Open Operations → Troubleshooting → Path Diagnostics in the sidebar (the Global, FortiWeb and FortiADC ADOMs; the FortiGate, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs do not list it).
  2. Choose the Appliance. Pick from the appliance lists what that device publishes; or type the name in Server policy / virtual server.
  3. Optionally set Log window (min) and Use SSH.
  4. Optionally override the endpoint: Published host, Port, Scheme, Path. Leave Published host empty to derive it from the policy's VIP. A typed host and port must be a pair the appliance publishes unless you hold monitoring.probe_free.
  5. Optionally pick FortiAnalyzer (layer 7) and its FAZ ADOM, FortiGate devid and VDOM.
  6. Click Walk the ladder.
  7. Read The ladder table (Layer, Vantage, Verdict, What it found) and the verdict above it.

Every field has a ? help popover on the page.

Configuration#

Walk form#

Field Description Required Example
Appliance FortiWeb or FortiADC in this ADOM Yes fweb-01
Server policy / virtual server Object to diagnose Yes pol-shop
Log window (min) Look-back for border flows and attack log; 1–1440 No 30
Use SSH Probe backends from the appliance too No off
Published host / Port / Scheme / Path Endpoint to test; empty host = derived from the VIP. A typed host and port the appliance does not publish needs <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#monitoring-probe_free" title="Probe free targets — Point the certificate inspector and the transaction tracer at a
host SATOM does not manage. Inventory destinations never need this.">monitoring.probe_free No shop.example.com / 443 / https / /
FortiAnalyzer (layer 7) Collector for border correlation No faz-01
FAZ ADOM / FortiGate devid / VDOM Selector for the border query No root

Site settings (Settings → Path Diagnostics → Settings)#

Setting Default Range
Path Diagnostics is available on —
Default look-back window (minutes) 30 1–1440
Front-door probe timeout (seconds) 8 1–30
Probe from the appliance by default off —
Default FortiAnalyzer ADOM root —
Default device id (devid) empty —
Default VDOM empty —
Rows per border query 200 1–1000
Border query timeout (seconds) 20 1–120

The judgement criteria (for example a phase must be ≥ 60 % of the request and ≥ 400 ms to be called dominant; certificates warn at 14 days) are displayed on the settings page but are not editable. Settings → Path Diagnostics → Architecture documents the ladder. The same on/off switch also controls the Upgrade Advisory (the firmware release-notes reviewer).

Example#

🧪Example — Users report a 502 on shop.example.com

Walk fweb-01 / pol-shop. Rungs 0–4 pass; rung 5 Pool passes; rung 6 Backends fails: 2 of 2 members unreachable from the appliance. Rungs 7–9 are not walked. The verdict reads Fault localised at layer 6 (Backends), observed from the appliance. Next step: check the servers and the network between the appliance and them.

Result#

  • Nothing is changed on any device.
  • Each walk writes an audit entry scout.walk with the appliance, object and the localised layer (or no fault localised).

Troubleshooting#

"Path Diagnostics is switched off for this site. An administrator can turn it back on under Settings → Path Diagnostics → Availability."#

Path Diagnostics is disabled; every Path Diagnostics URL answers 503. Turn it on in Settings → Path Diagnostics → Settings (Path Diagnostics is available). Nothing was deleted while it was off.

"Front-end refused: <host>:<port> is not published by this appliance. …"#

The full text continues Typing an arbitrary host or port needs the 'monitoring.probe_free' permission; leave Published host blank to use the object's VIP. You typed a host and port that is not one of the appliance's published pairs and you do not hold monitoring.probe_free. A host the appliance publishes is not enough: the port must be the one that address or service is served on.

Solution — leave Published host empty, type a host and port the appliance publishes, or ask an administrator for the permission.

"Pick an appliance this ADOM can see."#

No appliance selected, or it is not visible in this ADOM.

"Path Diagnostics needs the name of the server policy to diagnose."#

Fill Server policy / virtual server.

"Path Diagnostics walks a server policy or a virtual server. 'fortianalyzer' is not one of them …"#

Only FortiWeb and FortiADC appliances can be diagnosed.

Rung 7 (Path) is always "unknown"#

No FortiAnalyzer selected, or it is not reachable / retired (the picker lists retired and parked analysers with a flag). Select one and check its ADOM/devid.

A rung says "this rung raised while being walked"#

A Path Diagnostics defect, reported as could not look rather than as a fault in your path. Report it (Bug reports).

Path Diagnostics is missing from the menu#

Possible causes — your profile has no read permission, so you may not open Path Diagnostics; the entry is then hidden. (When Path Diagnostics is switched off for the site, the entry is not hidden: it is shown disabled with the reason.) Or you are looking for the old label: until 2026-10-14 this page was called Scout, and it sat under Operations → Troubleshooting (FortiWeb) or directly in Fleet (other ADOMs).

Solution — open Operations → Troubleshooting. If the entry is not there, ask an administrator for a read permission, for example monitoring.view.

Verification — Operations → Troubleshooting → Path Diagnostics appears in the sidebar.

Advanced#

Advanced Rules of the ladder
  • The first fail stops the walk; warn does not.
  • A rung that cannot run is unknown and counted as a blind spot.
  • Appliance health stops the walk only for capacity and deep-monitor signals; a stale harvest does not, because it describes SATOM's reach, not the data path.
  • Each rung records its vantage (this node, the appliance, the collector); the three are never merged.
  • Internally the page keeps its old identifier (scout): the URL, the blueprint, the settings keys and the audit action all still say scout.
